Energy Conservation Pendulum Simulation

This interactive 3D physics simulation demonstrates the law of conservation of energy using a pendulum. Students can explore the transformation between gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy, and thermal energy.

System Definition in Energy Conservation

A key idea in energy conservation is the definition of the system. For a pendulum, gravitational potential energy is not a property of the bob alone. It belongs to the interaction between the Earth and the pendulum bob. Therefore, the gravitational potential energy is defined for the Earth + bob system.

PE = mgh

Mechanical Energy Without Friction

When friction is zero, the pendulum continuously transforms energy between potential energy and kinetic energy. At the highest point, potential energy is maximum and kinetic energy is minimum. At the lowest point, kinetic energy is maximum and potential energy is minimum.

Emechanical = PE + KE = constant

Energy Conservation With Friction

When friction or air resistance is present, the mechanical energy of the pendulum decreases. However, the energy does not disappear. It is transferred to thermal energy by non-conservative work. For the larger system including the surroundings, the total energy remains conserved.

PE + KE + Ethermal = constant

What Students Learn

  • Potential Energy Requires a System

    Gravitational potential energy is associated with the Earth-bob interaction, not only the bob by itself.

  • Kinetic and Potential Energy Transform

    As the pendulum swings downward, potential energy decreases and kinetic energy increases. As it swings upward, kinetic energy decreases and potential energy increases.

  • Friction Transfers Energy

    Friction reduces mechanical energy, but the lost mechanical energy appears as thermal energy. This helps students understand non-conservative work.

  • Total Energy Is Conserved

    For the larger system including the Earth, bob, and surroundings, total energy remains constant even when mechanical energy decreases.

How to Use This Physics Simulation

  • Drag the pendulum bob away from equilibrium and release it.
  • Observe the exchange between PE and KE.
  • Increase friction and observe thermal energy increasing.
  • Change gravity to compare pendulum motion on different planets.
  • Change mass and compare energy values.
